question: Quanto costa in infrastruttura mesh-gateway?

context.heading: Timeouts
context.content:
`upstreamTimeoutMs` is the default upstream timeout and is 30000. A route can
override it with its own `timeoutMs`. `readHeaderTimeoutMs` is 5000 and
`idleTimeoutMs` is 120000.

context.heading: UpstreamProxy
context.content:
`UpstreamProxy` performs the forwarded call. It applies the per-route timeout,
retries idempotent methods and records the upstream latency metric
`gateway_upstream_duration_seconds`.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic
and no database.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

answer:
La documentazione fornita non riporta il costo di esercizio di mesh-gateway.

Le sezioni disponibili descrivono «Purpose», «Timeouts» e «UpstreamProxy», ma nessuna contiene questo dato.

Per rispondere servirebbe i dati di costo o il budget dell'infrastruttura.

question: Quali upstream sono raggiungibili tramite il gateway?

context.heading: Document routes
context.content:
`/v1/documents/*` forwards to the `docsync-platform` upstream. Provider callback
paths under `/v1/providers/callbacks/*` are declared with `authRequired: false`
because providers authenticate with a signature instead of a bearer token.

context.heading: Identity routes
context.content:
`/v1/me` and `/v1/auth/*` forward to the `acme-identity` upstream.
`/v1/me` requires authentication; `/v1/auth/login` does not.

context.heading: Billing routes
context.content:
`/v1/invoices/*` and `/v1/subscriptions/*` forward to the `billing-core`
upstream and require the caller to carry a billing scope.

answer:
Nelle sezioni fornite sono documentati tre upstream:

- `acme-identity`, per `/v1/me` e `/v1/auth/*`; `/v1/me` richiede autenticazione, `/v1/auth/login` no [03-routing.md — Identity routes].
- `billing-core`, per `/v1/invoices/*` e `/v1/subscriptions/*`, che richiedono uno scope billing [03-routing.md — Billing routes].
- `docsync-platform`, per `/v1/documents/*`; i path di callback dei provider sotto `/v1/providers/callbacks/*` sono dichiarati con `authRequired: false` perché i provider si autenticano con una firma invece che con un bearer token [03-routing.md — Document routes].

question: Perché il rate limiter usa Redis?

context.heading: Kubernetes
context.content:
The gateway is deployed as a Deployment with 4 replicas and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler
targeting 60% CPU. The Service is of type LoadBalancer. Config is mounted from
the `mesh-gateway-config` ConfigMap; `routes.yaml` lives in the same ConfigMap.

context.heading: RateLimiter
context.content:
`RateLimiter` is a token bucket keyed by caller id and route. Buckets live in
Redis so all gateway replicas share the same budget. When the bucket is empty
the request is rejected with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header.

answer:
Perché il budget deve essere condiviso fra le repliche: `RateLimiter` è un token bucket per caller id e rotta, e i bucket vivono in Redis proprio perché tutte le repliche del gateway condividano lo stesso budget. Quando il bucket è vuoto la richiesta viene rifiutata con HTTP 429 e un header `Retry-After` [02-architecture.md — RateLimiter].

Il gateway è effettivamente multi-replica: è deployato come Deployment con 4 repliche e un HorizontalPodAutoscaler al 60% di CPU [07-deployment.md — Kubernetes].

question: Come viene gestita una richiesta dal gateway?

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic
and no database.

context.heading: Request pipeline
context.content:
Each request passes through the pipeline in order: `TLSTerminator`,
`RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`,
`UpstreamProxy`. A middleware that rejects a request short circuits the rest of
the pipeline.

answer:
Ogni richiesta attraversa la pipeline in ordine: `TLSTerminator`, `RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`, `UpstreamProxy`. Un middleware che rifiuta la richiesta corto-circuita il resto della pipeline [02-architecture.md — Request pipeline].

Il gateway termina TLS, autentica il chiamante, applica i rate limit e inoltra la richiesta al servizio upstream corretto; non contiene logica di business né database [01-overview.md — Purpose].

context.content:

If deliveries exist, `GET /documents/{id}/deliveries` shows the provider, the

context.content:

a day later and the fourth three days later.

question: Come vengono risolte le rotte?

context.heading: Queue
context.content:
Long running work is pushed to Redis and consumed by `billing-worker`. Invoice
issuing, dunning emails and webhook replays are queued. The queue is at-least
once: every consumer must be idempotent.

context.heading: routes.yaml
context.content:
Each entry declares `path`, `methods`, `upstream`, `timeoutMs`, `authRequired`
and `rateLimit`. The first matching entry wins, so more specific paths must be
declared before wildcards.

context.heading: webhook_events
context.content:
`webhook_events` stores every received Stripe event with `provider_event_id`
(unique), `type`, `payload`, `processed_at`. The unique index on
`provider_event_id` is what makes webhook processing idempotent.

context.heading: POST /invoices
context.content:
Creates a draft invoice for a subscription. Body: `{ subscriptionId, lines }`.
Returns HTTP 201 with the invoice in `draft` status. Creating an invoice does
not charge anything.

context.heading: RouteResolver
context.content:
`RouteResolver` matches the request path against the route table and produces an
upstream target. The route table is loaded from `routes.yaml` at startup and
refreshed on SIGHUP. An unmatched path returns HTTP 404 `route_not_found`
without contacting any upstream.

answer:
`RouteResolver` confronta il path della richiesta con la route table e produce un target upstream. La tabella viene caricata da `routes.yaml` all'avvio e ricaricata su SIGHUP; un path senza corrispondenza restituisce HTTP 404 `route_not_found` senza contattare nessun upstream [02-architecture.md — RouteResolver].

Ogni voce di `routes.yaml` dichiara `path`, `methods`, `upstream`, `timeoutMs`, `authRequired` e `rateLimit`, e vince la prima corrispondenza: i path più specifici vanno dichiarati prima dei wildcard [03-routing.md — routes.yaml].

question: Che cosa restituisce il gateway se l'upstream va in timeout?

context.heading: Upstream errors
context.content:
`upstream_timeout` (HTTP 504) when the upstream exceeds the route timeout.
`upstream_unavailable` (HTTP 502) when the connection fails. The gateway never
converts an upstream 5xx into a 2xx: upstream status codes above 499 are passed
through unchanged, with the body replaced by the gateway error envelope.

context.heading: A provider was never called
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` rejects a delivery before calling any provider when the channel
has no mapping in `docsync.channels`. In that case the delivery is recorded with
`unsupported_channel` and no `provider_message_id` is present.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
`{ "error": "<code>", "requestId": "<id>" }`. The `requestId` matches the
`X-Request-Id` header and is the key to correlate gateway and upstream logs.

context.heading: Property sources
context.content:
Configuration lives in `application.yaml` and is overridden per environment by
`application-{profile}.yaml` and by environment variables. Spring relaxed
binding applies: `docsync.render.timeout-ms` can be set as
`DOCSYNC_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS`.

context.heading: Access tokens
context.content:
Access tokens are short lived. The platform standard is a 60 minute access
token lifetime, and Acme Identity follows the platform standard.

answer:
HTTP 504 con codice `upstream_timeout`, quando l'upstream supera il timeout della rotta [06-errors.md — Upstream errors].

Il corpo segue l'envelope standard `{ "error": "<code>", "requestId": "<id>" }`, dove `requestId` coincide con l'header `X-Request-Id` ed è la chiave per correlare i log del gateway con quelli dell'upstream [06-errors.md — Error envelope].

Nota: un fallimento di connessione è invece `upstream_unavailable` con HTTP 502, e il gateway non converte mai un 5xx dell'upstream in un 2xx [06-errors.md — Upstream errors].

question: Qual è la differenza tra un 502 e un 504 restituiti dal gateway?

context.heading: Upstream errors
context.content:
`upstream_timeout` (HTTP 504) when the upstream exceeds the route timeout.
`upstream_unavailable` (HTTP 502) when the connection fails. The gateway never
converts an upstream 5xx into a 2xx: upstream status codes above 499 are passed
through unchanged, with the body replaced by the gateway error envelope.

answer:
Riguardano due fallimenti diversi della chiamata upstream [06-errors.md — Upstream errors]:

- HTTP 504 `upstream_timeout`: l'upstream ha superato il timeout della rotta.
- HTTP 502 `upstream_unavailable`: la connessione verso l'upstream è fallita.

In nessuno dei due casi il gateway maschera l'esito: gli status code dell'upstream sopra il 499 vengono propagati invariati, con il body sostituito dall'envelope di errore del gateway [06-errors.md — Upstream errors].

answer:
Il 404 documentato del gateway è `route_not_found`, restituito quando nessuna rotta corrisponde al path, senza contattare alcun upstream [02-architecture.md — RouteResolver].

Verifiche che derivano dalla documentazione:
1. Ordine delle voci in `routes.yaml`: vince la prima corrispondenza, quindi una voce wildcard dichiarata prima di una più specifica può intercettare il path [03-routing.md — routes.yaml].
2. Corrispondenza di `path` e `methods` della voce, che sono entrambi dichiarati per ogni rotta [03-routing.md — routes.yaml].

context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.content:
DocSync generates, signs and delivers documents (contracts, certificates,
policy files) to end users. It is a Java 21 Spring Boot service. Documents are
produced from templates, stored in object storage and delivered through one of
several delivery providers.

answer:
Tramite il request id.

- L'envelope di errore del gateway contiene `requestId`, che coincide con l'header `X-Request-Id` ed è la chiave per correlare i log del gateway con quelli dell'upstream [06-errors.md — Error envelope].

context.heading: invoices
context.content:
`invoices` holds `id`, `subscription_id`, `number`, `currency`, `amount_cents`,

context.content:

2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into

3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

context.content:

mapping lives in `UserRepository.toDomain` and `ProfileRepository.toDomain`.
`display_name` in the database is `displayName` in the API payload.

question: What does the readiness probe check?

context.heading: Components
context.content:
`InvoiceService` builds invoices from subscription and usage records.
`PaymentService` executes charges and refunds. `StripeGateway` is the only
component that performs HTTP calls to Stripe. `WebhookHandler` consumes Stripe
callbacks. `SubscriptionRepository`, `InvoiceRepository` and `PaymentRepository`
own database access.

context.heading: Health
context.content:
`/healthz` is the liveness probe and checks only the process. `/readyz` is the
readiness probe and additionally checks the Redis connection used by
`RateLimiter`.

context.heading: Naming
context.content:
Database columns are snake_case. The API layer maps them to camelCase; the
mapping lives in `UserRepository.toDomain` and `ProfileRepository.toDomain`.
`display_name` in the database is `displayName` in the API payload.

context.heading: StripeGateway
context.content:
`StripeGateway` wraps the Stripe SDK. It exposes `create_payment_intent`,
`capture`, `refund` and `retrieve_event`. It is the single integration point
with Stripe: `PaymentService` calls `StripeGateway`, never the SDK. The gateway
adds the idempotency key and translates Stripe errors into domain errors.

context.heading: RateLimiter
context.content:

question: Come viene gestita una richiesta dal gateway?

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic

context.heading: Request pipeline
context.content:
Each request passes through the pipeline in order: `TLSTerminator`,
`RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`,
`UpstreamProxy`. A middleware that rejects a request short circuits the rest of
the pipeline.

context.heading: GET /users/:id
context.content:
Internal route, requires the `users:read` scope. Returns the same shape as
`GET /me` for an arbitrary account id. Used by other services.

context.heading: Issuing failures
context.content:
Issuing can fail before any charge: the invoice is not in `draft` state, the
number allocation conflicts (unique violation on `invoices.number`), or the PDF
render step fails and the job is retried by the worker. A failed issue leaves
the invoice in `draft`.

context.heading: POST /providers/callbacks/{provider}
context.content:
Endpoint used by delivery providers to report status changes. Handled by
`DeliveryStatusListener`. The payload is provider specific and normalised into
the `deliveries.status` values.

answer:
Ogni richiesta attraversa la pipeline in ordine: `TLSTerminator`, `RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`, `UpstreamProxy`. Un middleware che rifiuta la richiesta corto-circuita il resto della pipeline [02-architecture.md — Request pipeline].

Il gateway termina TLS, autentica il chiamante, applica i rate limit e inoltra la richiesta al servizio upstream corretto; non contiene logica di business né database [01-overview.md — Purpose].

question: I servizi interni sono raggiungibili direttamente dall'esterno?

context.heading: Purpose

context.heading: PATCH /me
context.content:
Updates profile fields only. Accepts any subset of `displayName`, `avatarUrl`,
`locale`, `timezone`. Account fields such as `email` and `status` are not
editable through this route. Returns the updated `CurrentUser` payload.

context.heading: Position in the platform

context.heading: Current User Flow
context.content:
1. The client calls `GET /me` with a bearer token.
2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

If the profile row is missing, step 5 returns the default profile, so
`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.heading: Sources
context.content:
Configuration is read at boot by `config/loadConfig.ts`. Values come from
environment variables, with defaults declared in `config/defaults.ts`. There is
no runtime reload: changing configuration requires a restart.

answer:
No. I client parlano solo con il gateway e i servizi interni non sono raggiungibili dall'esterno del cluster [01-overview.md — Position in the platform].

Il gateway è l'unico ingress per ogni chiamata API pubblica: termina TLS, autentica il chiamante, applica i rate limit e inoltra al servizio upstream [01-overview.md — Purpose].

question: What does the readiness probe check?

context.heading: Health
context.content:
`/healthz` is the liveness probe and checks only the process. `/readyz` is the
readiness probe and additionally checks the Redis connection used by
`RateLimiter`.

context.heading: RateLimiter
context.content:
`RateLimiter` is a token bucket keyed by caller id and route. Buckets live in
Redis so all gateway replicas share the same budget. When the bucket is empty
the request is rejected with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header.

answer:
`/readyz` is the readiness probe and, on top of the process check, it verifies the Redis connection used by `RateLimiter` [07-deployment.md — Health].

`/healthz` is the liveness probe and only checks the process [07-deployment.md — Health]. The Redis dependency is real because the rate limiter keeps its token buckets there so every replica shares one budget [02-architecture.md — RateLimiter].

question: In quale versione è stato introdotto Timeouts?

context.heading: Request pipeline
context.content:
Each request passes through the pipeline in order: `TLSTerminator`,
`RequestIdMiddleware`, `AuthMiddleware`, `RateLimiter`, `RouteResolver`,
`UpstreamProxy`. A middleware that rejects a request short circuits the rest of
the pipeline.

context.heading: Timeouts
context.content:
`upstreamTimeoutMs` is the default upstream timeout and is 30000. A route can
override it with its own `timeoutMs`. `readHeaderTimeoutMs` is 5000 and
`idleTimeoutMs` is 120000.

question: I servizi interni sono raggiungibili direttamente dall'esterno?

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Mesh Gateway is the single ingress for every public API call at Acme. It is a Go
service that terminates TLS, authenticates the caller, applies rate limits and
forwards the request to the right upstream service. It holds no business logic
and no database.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

answer:
No. I client parlano solo con il gateway e i servizi interni non sono raggiungibili dall'esterno del cluster [01-overview.md — Position in the platform].

Il gateway è l'unico ingress per ogni chiamata API pubblica: termina TLS, autentica il chiamante, applica i rate limit e inoltra al servizio upstream [01-overview.md — Purpose].
